teaching_structure.teaching_activities: The teacher holds up a beaker of water with a few drops of amino acid solution (coloured for effect) and says, This is not soup you would eat.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students recall that Pasteur showed life only comes from life. But the very first life must have come from non‑life through a process called chemical evolution.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: The teacher uses a large diagram to explain the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis: a reducing atmosphere (methane, ammonia, hydrogen, water vapour) + energy sources - organic monomers (amino acids, sugars) - polymers (proteins, RNA) - protobionts (coacervates) - first primitive cells.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students copy the flow chart of chemical evolution into their notebooks. They label the Miller‑Urey apparatus: flask for atmosphere,  spark electrodes, condenser, trap for ocean.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Scientific report of the project is clearly written and quality project product(s) are obtained
